title: Blood Agar (Sheep Blood Agar)

references.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

purpose: Supports growth of many fastidious organisms via the blood-enriched base, and differentiates organisms by their hemolytic pattern (alpha, beta, or gamma hemolysis).
targetOrganisms: Many fastidious and non-fastidious bacteria; commonly used for Streptococcus and Staphylococcus species differentiation by hemolysis

formulations.sourceLabel: Typical preparation: TSA base + 5% defibrinated sheep blood

reference.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

compositionPerLiter.amount: commonly 5% v/v, added after the base is autoclaved and cooled

finalPh.value: approximately 7.3 ± 0.2 for the base agar before blood addition

preparationSummary: Prepare and autoclave the agar base, cool to approximately 45–50°C (a temperature the brief flags as needing verification against the specific base/blood product, not treated as a fixed universal number here), then aseptically add sterile defibrinated blood and mix gently before pouring, to avoid lysing red cells or introducing bubbles.

sterilization.value: the agar base is autoclaved before blood is added; blood itself is not autoclaved (heat would hemolyze/denature it)
sterilization.dependsOn: base medium only — blood is added aseptically post-sterilization

storage: Refrigerate prepared plates in sealed bags; protect from excessive drying.

shelfLife.value: manufacturer-stated; varies by product and blood source

expectedAppearance: Opaque, reddish-brown agar from the blood content.
qualityControl: Confirm hemolytic patterns using known reference organisms for alpha, beta, and gamma hemolysis before relying on differentiation.

reactions.organismOrGroup: Alpha-hemolytic organisms (e.g. Streptococcus pneumoniae, viridans streptococci)

reactions.reaction: No change to the surrounding blood agar

manufacturerNotes: Hemolysis patterns can differ visually depending on the animal blood source used (sheep vs. horse, for instance) — confirm which blood source a given protocol/reference assumes.
